name: application-feature-flag-table
title: Feature Flag Table
description: Feature flag matrix with a toggle per environment column and an optional rollout percentage, driven by a typed environments/rows prop contract.
useWhen: An internal admin tool needs to manage multiple feature flags across multiple environments (dev, staging, production) at once.
Some flags are in partial rollout and need a visible percentage alongside their enabled state.
You want a single reusable flag-matrix primitive instead of one toggle-row component per flag.
avoidWhen: You only manage a single flag in a single context — use the simpler Feature Flag Toggle Row instead.
Flags need per-user or per-segment targeting rules — pair this table with a dedicated targeting rule editor.
There is only one environment — a flat list of toggles is simpler than a matrix table.
responsiveBehavior: The table scrolls horizontally on narrow viewports via its wrapping overflow container; each environment column stays a fixed minimum width so the toggle switches remain tappable.
accessibility: Each toggle uses role='switch' with aria-checked reflecting state, plus a composed aria-label naming the flag, environment, and rollout percentage when applicable.
The rollout percentage is rendered as visible text beneath the toggle, not conveyed by switch position alone.
Flag keys render in a monospace <code> element to distinguish them as identifiers rather than prose.

variants.title: Feature Flag Table
variants.description: Flag matrix with Dev/Staging/Production columns, per-environment toggle switches, and a visible rollout percentage for a partially-enabled flag.
accessibility: Toggle switches carry aria-checked and a full descriptive aria-label including the rollout percentage when relevant.

variants.title: Feature Flag Table (Dark)
variants.description: Feature flag matrix adapted for dark surfaces with the same environment-column, toggle, and rollout structure.
accessibility: Toggle track/thumb colors and rollout percentage text must meet WCAG AA contrast on dark surfaces.
